checks.label: For a three-phase generator, three coils of wire are placed at angles of 120° to each other: the three phase voltage arrows are drawn equal, 230 V each, 120° apart, and so are the three 10 A star currents
UK mains electricity operates at a nominal voltage of 230V: the voltmeter across one winding reads V_ph = 230 V, and every star current drawn is 230 ÷ 23 = 10 A

In balanced Y circuits, line voltage is equal to phase voltage times the square root of 3, while line current is equal to phase current: the bold arrow is 1.732 times a phase arrow, landing on the voltmeter's 398.4 V between L1 and L2, and the clamp on L1 reads the 10 A each phase carries

The line voltage can be found by taking the phasor sum of the voltage in two phases of the source: the bold arrow closes L1's arrow and L2's turned half round, laid on L1's tip, and is turned 30° from L1's
The neutral conductor carries no current in a balanced three-phase network: three 10 A currents laid tip to tail close a triangle, so no neutral arrow is left and the neutral clamp reads 0.0 A
Unbalance: at every L3 current from 0 to 10 A the neutral arrow closes the gap and is 10 A minus L3's current (4.0 A at 6 A, 3.0 A at 7 A, 10.0 A with L3 off), and the clamp and the model agree

P T = √3 V L I L cosθ where cosθ is the power factor: in star and in delta the readout 3 × V_ph × I_ph × cos φ equals √3 × V_L × I_L × cos φ (5520 W and 16,561 W; the heaters 1725 W and 5175 W), every readout worked from the factors it shows; on the board √3 × 400 × 20 = 13,856 VA, of which 11,778 W at 0.85

The average power can be expressed as P avg = VI cosφ: one load's drawn voltage and current are each √3 times longer in delta, the angle between them stays 36.9°, and V_ph × I_ph × cos φ goes from 1840 W to 5520 W, a third of each readout

Delta: L1's bold arrow is load L1–L2's current minus load L3–L1's, 17.32 × √3 = 30.0 A and 12 × √3 = 20.8 A, which the clamp on L1 reads; and for the motor two 15.0 A winding currents differ by the clamp's 26 A
A sine peaks at √2 times its rms: the 400 V rms line voltage is drawn with its rms level at 400 V and, after a right answer, a peak arrow of 400 × 1.414 = 566 V
